port.about: Port of the local page, which only ever listens on 127.0.0.1. $CAKE_PORT overrides it.

site_key.about: Made on first start; the page script sends it with every visit.

site_domain.about: Your website's domain, without https:// (setup --print --site, or the settings page): uploads from another site are kept but left out of the dashboard.

framework.about: Your website's framework, as setup --print --site detected it.

site_url.about: A page of your website that doctor opens to check that it loads cake.js and that its response carries the server half's token, e.g. http://localhost:3000/ for a dev server or https://example.com/ for the live site; empty: doctor reads the site's files only (setup --print --site).

register_url.about: Where the local dashboard's registration card sends your registration, once, when you press "Register & Continue" (PRIVACY.md, "Registration"); nothing else is ever sent there. Empty: nothing is sent, and the card says so and asks again the next time you open the dashboard.

mask_inputs.about: Retired: cake.js always masks what visitors type (agentcake/data/privacy.json), so this can no longer be set; kept so that `config set mask_inputs` says why (the settings page has no such switch since S5.5).

hook_dom.about: cake.js wraps your site's own document lookups (document.querySelector, getElementById and the like, data/cakejs.json env.hook) to notice an automation framework calling them, which catches some extensions. It changes functions your pages call, so it is off unless you turn it on.

hide_selectors.about: CSS selectors, comma-separated, of parts of your pages cake.js never records, on top of its own private elements (data/privacy.json): a replay shows an empty box of their size, and nothing typed into them is kept. Empty: only cake.js's own.

retention_days.about: 0 keeps every session; 30 or 90 deletes whole sessions older than that.

budget_mb.about: Disk budget of the database: half of the 20 GB disk of the smallest server SERVER.md describes (Debian takes about 3 GB, and SQLite needs room to grow), and small next to any laptop's free space.

budget_warn_ratio.about: From this share of the budget the dashboard and settings warn.

budget_pace_days.about: Days of recent growth used to tell when the budget will be full.

auto_free.about: Free space by removing old replays: when the budget is full, those of the oldest human-only sessions; when the disk has less than disk_min_free_mb free, the oldest ones of any session, human-only sessions first, so that new replays are still stored. Off: new replays stop instead.

auto_free_target_ratio.about: Freeing space stops at this share of the budget.

auto_free_quiet_ms.about: A session with activity this recently is never freed.

auto_free_batch_sessions.about: Sessions whose replays are removed per round while freeing space; below disk_min_free_mb a round goes with a collected batch, at most once a maintenance tick unless the last round removed this many.

disk_min_free_mb.about: With less free space than this on the disk that holds the data folder, the oldest replays are removed until there is this much again (with what the next maintenance round gives back), human-only sessions first, then any session without activity for auto_free_quiet_ms, and new replays are still stored. When removing all of those would still leave less than this free (other files fill the disk), none is removed. Then, or with auto_free off, new replays stop until there is room and doctor, the settings page and /api/health say why. Visits, verdicts and the input timing they are made from are always recorded. 0 turns the check off.

public_listen.about: Server mode: host:port of the public listener; empty turns server mode off.

path_prefix.about: Server mode: the path of your site the public listener answers under, e.g. /cake.

trust_lb.about: Server mode: read the visitor's address, country, TLS fingerprint and protocol from the load balancer's headers.

ip_salt_days.about: Server mode: days one salt of the visitors' address hashes is used; then a new one replaces it and the old hashes can no longer be linked to an address.

public_max_body_bytes.about: Largest POST the public listener reads; a larger one is refused unread.

local_max_body_bytes.about: Largest POST body the local listener reads, and the most a gzipped upload may unzip to on either listener (cake.js's largest record is 4 MiB).

public_script_cache_s.about: How long browsers may keep cake.js and the recorder from the public listener.

max_events_per_session.about: Records kept per session in each stream (rrweb replay, raw input, signals) at most; later ones are refused and counted.

max_events_per_post.about: Records one upload may hold (rrweb events, raw input and signals together); an upload with more is refused and counted. cake.js sends at most 51,200 characters per batch.

public_judge_interval_ms.about: Server mode: a session is judged at most this often while it sends (and whenever a page of it is opened).

judge_interval_ms.about: On this computer: a session that keeps sending is judged at most this often (opening a page of it judges it at once); 0 judges every batch.

judge_quiet_s.about: A session that sends nothing for this long is judged once more and its verdict is final; new data opens it again.

stale_judge_batch_sessions.about: Sessions judged before a page is drawn, latest first.

handoff_lead_ms.about: The replay's "Jump to hand-off" starts this long before the hand-off, so the human's last moves show first.

token_max_age_ms.about: A server-half token older than this is stale.

token_max_future_ms.about: How far ahead of this computer's clock a token's time may be (a site's clock may run ahead).

log_match_window_s.about: Log import: a page request in your web server's log belongs to the page view whose first upload came from the same address (hashed) and User-Agent at most this many seconds after it.

log_match_skew_s.about: Log import: how many seconds a page view's first upload may seem to arrive before its page request was logged, for when the web server's clock and Agent Cake's differ a little.

db_timeout_s.about: How long a database write waits for another one to finish.

health_timeout_s.about: How long status and start wait for the running server to answer.

http_timeout_s.about: How long doctor and ping wait for each local page.

delete_timeout_s.about: How long `agentcake delete` waits for a running cake to delete: it rewrites the database file, which takes a while when the file is large.

start_wait_s.about: How long start waits for the new background server to answer.

start_poll_s.about: How often start asks whether the new background server answers.

stop_wait_s.about: How long stop waits for the background server to exit once asked to (it takes about half a second); the grace period `docker stop` gives a container.

stop_poll_s.about: How often stop asks whether the background server has exited.
